 Coram:Honourable Mr. Justice Hasmukh D. Suthar

Date : 13/03/2026
 Oral Judgment

1. By way of present application the applicant seeks the following relief:
"c Your Lordships may be pleased to quash and set aside the judgment and order passed below Exh.31 in Criminal Appeal No.12 of 2012 dated 05/02/2013 by the State Of Gujarat vs Yogeshbhai Lilachandbhai Sheth on 13 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7414807/
1 learned Additional Sessions Judge, S.K., Himmatnagar and further be pleased to confirm judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 19/01/2012 passed by the learned 6th Additional Senior Civil Judge & Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Himmatnagar passed in Criminal Case No.284 of 2003;."
2. Brief facts of the case are that the original complainant, a Food Inspector, visited the shop of the respondent-original NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/534/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/03/2026 undefined accused and purchased a sample of Mohanthal.
After completing the necessary formalities of packing, sealing, and drawing the panchnama, the sample was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis.

The Public Analyst reported that the sample did not conform to the prescribed standards under the Act and Rules, as the percentage of Tartrazine Yellow colour was found to be higher than the permissible limit.
After obtaining the necessary sanction, the complainant lodged a complaint.

Upon recording the evidence of the complainant and the panch witness and after conclusion of the trial, the learned Magistrate held the accused guilty of offences under Sections 2(1-a)(a), (j) and (m) read with Sections 7(1) and 7(5) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954, punishable under Section 16(1) of the Act.

entities.text: Sections 2(1-a)(a), (j) and (m) read with Sections 7(1) and 7(5)
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: The accused was sentenced to six months' simple imprisonment and a fine of Rs.2,000/-, and in default, to undergo one month's simple imprisonment.

3. Learned APP appearing for the applicant-State submits that the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Himmatnagar, was pleased to convict the accused; however, the learned Appellate Court has overturned the said finding without assigning sufficient and cogent reasons, despite there being sufficient evidence available on record.
It is further submitted that the order passed by the learned Appellate Court is ex facie illegal and arbitrary.
It is submitted that the prescribed sanction was duly obtained, and the relevant evidence was produced at Exhibit 26.

The report of the Public Analyst was also supplied to the accused, and the receipt in that regard is produced on record; however, the learned Appellate Court failed to properly appreciate the same and, taking a hyper-technical view,
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/534/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/03/2026 undefined acquitted the accused.

It is further submitted that while drawing the sample, the mandatory procedure prescribed under Section 14 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act was duly complied with,
which aspect has also not been properly considered by the learned Appellate Court.
The sample of Mohanthal was found to be adulterated and not in conformity with the prescribed standards under the provisions of the Act.
Therefore, it is submitted that the learned Trial Court has not committed any error in convicting the accused; however, the learned Appellate Court has erred in allowing the appeal.
Hence, the learned APP has requested that the present appeal be allowed.

4. Having heard the learned Additional Public Prosecutor, it appears that the sample of Mohanthal came to be drawn and the appeal has been filed mainly on the ground of breach of Rule 14,
contending that there was no compliance with Rule 14 and that the bottles used for collecting the sample were not clean.
It is further submitted that there was permissible mixture and that after drawing the sample, compliance with Rule 14 has not been proved on record.

Except for the aforesaid aspects, the learned Appellate Court has relied upon the decisions in Gangadhar Yaswant Ramekar v. Mukeshbhai B. Shah, 2007 (2) FAC 190 and State of Gujarat v. Kaushikkumar J. Doshi,
(1999) 2 GCD 292.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the breach of Rule 14 and in the absence of any evidence regarding the testing of the sample, it is noted that the sample was drawn on 29th August 2002 and was sent for NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/534/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/03/2026 undefined analysis in January 2003.
Thereafter, no opportunity for re- analysis was extended to the accused.

In view of the aforesaid facts and the long gap between the drawing of the sample and its analysis, the report produced below Exhibit 42, and in the absence of any material showing supply of the copy of the Public Analyst's report, the breach of Section 13(2) has adversely affected the valuable right of the accused.
6. It appears that the learned Appellate Court has considered the fact that, in view of the violation of Section 13(2), the Public Analyst's report was not provided to the accused.
In the absence of proof of delivery of such report, the valuable right of the accused has been violated.

Therefore, in the absence of any such evidence, the learned Sessions Judge has not committed any error in light of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Vijendra v. State of Uttar Pradesh, AIR 2019 SC 4351.
7.

entities.text: Vijendra v. State of Uttar Pradesh, AIR 2019 SC 4351
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further prosecution failed to prove the authority of the food inspector and in absence of any evidence of the authority under Section 20 sanction is granted mechanically and learned Appellate Court come to the conclusion that the sanction was mechanical and relying on the decision of State of Gujarat v. Prajapati Amrut Natwarlal, 2008 1 GLH 631, extended the benefit of doubt to the accused and considering the breach of mandatory provision acquittal was recorded.
8.

entities.text: State of Gujarat v. Prajapati Amrut Natwarlal, 2008 1 GLH 631
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, no interference is required in the order passed by the learned Sessions Judge and the same does NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/534/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/03/2026 undefined not call for any interference with the findings recorded by the Sessions Court.
Hence, the present Revision Application stands dismissed.
